triggers.description: Returns 1 if a player with the specified ID number exists, 0 otherwise. This ID number is obtained using the `ID` trigger (see ID). Do not confuse PlayerID with TargetID.
triggers.args: **ID_number** An expression that evaluates to the ID number to check for (int)
triggers.example:
trigger1 = PlayerIDExist(var(4))  
; Triggers if a player with an ID number equal to the value of  
  var(4) exists.

triggers.name: PlayerIndexExist
triggers.description: Returns 1 if a player with the specified index number exists, 0 otherwise. See [PlayerIndex](redirections#playerindexn-new).
triggers.example: trigger1 = PlayerIndexExist(2)

triggers.name: PlayerNo
triggers.description: Returns character's player number. Player 1 side uses odd numbers (1, 3, 5, 7), player 2 side even numbers (2, 4, 6, 8). Stage [AttachedChar](https://github.com/ikemen-engine/Ikemen-GO/wiki/Stage-features#info_attachedchar) uses number outside maximum player range (9).
triggers.example: trigger1 = PlayerNo < 3

triggers.name: PlayerNoExist
triggers.description: Evaluates if the specified player number is currently in use.
triggers.args: player_number An expression that evaluates to the player number to check for (int)
triggers.example:
trigger1 = PlayerNoExist(3); Returns true if there's a player number 3
trigger1 = Player(3), Alive

triggers.name: Pos
triggers.description: Gets the value of the player's position. You must specify the component that you want to check, eg. `Pos Y` to check the Y-position.
triggers.details: For Pos X, the value is relative to the center of the screen (value 0). Negative is left, positive is right. Due to historical reasons, "Pos X" does not return absolute position of the player (i.e. relative to the center of the stage), which may be the more intuitive behavior. To get the absolute position of the player, use Pos X + CameraPos X. For Pos Y, the value is relative to the floor. Negative is higher up, positive is below the floor.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = Pos Y >= 0  
; True when the player is below the floor.

triggers.name: Power
triggers.description: Returns the amount of power the player has.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = power >= 1000  
; True if player has at least 1000 power (level 1).

triggers.name: PowerMax
triggers.description: Returns the maximum amount of power the player can have. This is normally 3000 (level 3).
triggers.example:
trigger1 = power < powermax / 2  
; True if player has less than half his maximum power.

triggers.name: PrevAnim
triggers.description: Returns the number of the anim that the player was last in.
triggers.example: trigger1 = PrevAnim = 200

triggers.name: PrevMoveType
triggers.description: Returns the MoveType that the player was last in.
triggers.args: [oper] =, != (other operators not valid) move_type (char) move_type to compare against: A, I, H (Attack, Idle and GetHit move-types respectively)
triggers.example: trigger1 = PrevMoveType = H

triggers.name: PrevStateNo
triggers.description: Returns the number of the state that the player was last in. The results of this trigger are not guaranteed to be accurate.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = PrevStateNo = [200,650]  
; Returns true if the player's last state number is between 200 and 650, inclusive.

triggers.name: PrevStateType
triggers.description: Returns the StateType that the player was last in.
triggers.args: [oper] =, != (other operators not valid) state_type (char) state_type to compare against: S, C, A, L (Stand, Crouch, Air and Liedown respectively)
triggers.example: trigger1 = PrevStateType = C

triggers.name: ProjCancelTime
triggers.description: This trigger takes an required nonnegative ID number as an argument. If the player's last projectile to make any kind of contact was cancelled by an opponent's projectile and had the specified ID number, then ProjCancelTime returns the number of ticks since that contact occurred. If the specified ID number is 0, then the projectile ID is not checked. If no projectile meets all the above conditions, then ProjCancelTime returns -1.
triggers.args: **exprn** Expression evaluating to a nonnegative ID number (int).
triggers.example:
trigger1 = ProjCancelTime(1234) = 1
; Triggers if a projectile with ID 1234 was just cancelled by an opponent's projectile.

trigger1 = ProjCancelTime(0) != -1 && ProjCancelTime(0) < 15
; Triggers if any of the player's projectiles were cancelled within last 15 ticks.

triggers.name: ProjClsnOverlap
triggers.description: Returns true if the projectile's collision box (either Clsn1 or Clsn2) overlaps with another player's collision boxes. This trigger uses Ikemen's internal collision detection, so it will work even with angled and rescaled boxes. If you want to specify a projectile with a specific projID, create a loop process that combines the projID with ProjVar.
triggers.args: index An index number based on all projectiles owned by the player. The index is equivalent to the index when -1 is specified for the ID in ProjVar. playerID The ID of the player against which to check the overlap box_type The target's collision box type. Valid values are Clsn1, Clsn2, Size and Dummy (nightly build only)
triggers.example: trigger1 = ProjClsnOverlap(var(3), p2,ID, clsn2)

triggers.name: ProjContact
triggers.description: This trigger takes an optional ID number as a suffix. If the ID number is omitted, ProjContact returns true if any of the player's projectiles either successfully hit the opponent or were guarded by the opponent. When the ID number is specified, ProjContact returns true only if any of the player's projectiles with the specified ID number either successfully hit the opponent or was guarded.
triggers.details: ProjContact will trigger once for each hit of the projectile, so a multi-hit projectile can trigger multiple times. The first form of ProjContact shown above is only valid for one tick after contact, unlike MoveContact. For the second form, ProjContact returns true if the projectile made contact n ticks ago, where n is a nonnegative number satisfying the relation "n [oper] value2". Specifying an ID number of 0 gives the same behavior as if the ID number is omitted (check all projectiles).
triggers.example:
trigger1 = ProjContact1234 = 1
; Triggers if a projectile with ID 1234 just made contact with the opponent.  

trigger1 = ProjContact456 = 0, < 15
; Triggers if no projectile with ID 456 made contact in the last 15 ticks.

triggers.name: ProjContactTime
triggers.description: This trigger takes an required nonnegative ID number as an argument. If the player's last projectile to make any kind of contact, made contact with the opponent and had the specified ID number, then ProjContactTime returns the number of ticks since that contact occurred. If the specified ID number is 0, then the projectile ID is not checked. If no projectile meets all the above conditions, then ProjContactTime returns -1.
triggers.args: **exprn** Expression evaluating to a nonnegative ID number (int).
triggers.example:
trigger1 = ProjContactTime(1234) = 1  
; Triggers if a projectile with ID 1234 just made contact with the opponent.

trigger1 = ProjContactTime(0) != -1 && ProjContactTime(0) < 15  
; Triggers if any of the player's projectiles made successful contact with the opponent within the last 15 ticks.

triggers.name: ProjGuarded
triggers.description: This trigger takes an optional ID number as a suffix. If the ID number is omitted, ProjGuarded returns true if any of the player's projectiles were guarded by the opponent. When the ID number is specified, ProjGuarded returns true only if one of the player's projectiles with the specified ID number was guarded by the opponent.
triggers.details: ProjGuarded will trigger once for each hit of the projectile, so a multi-hit projectile can trigger multiple times. The first form of ProjGuarded shown above is only valid for one tick after hit, unlike MoveGuarded. For the second form, ProjGuarded returns true if the projectile was guarded n ticks ago, where n is a nonnegative number satisfying the relation "n [oper] value2". Specifying an ID number of 0 gives the same behavior as if the ID number is omitted (check all projectiles).
triggers.example:
trigger1 = ProjGuarded1234 = 1
; Triggers if the opponent just blocked a projectile with ID 1234.

trigger1 = ProjGuarded = 1, < 15
; Triggers if the opponent blocked any projectile in the last 15 ticks.

triggers.name: ProjGuardedTime
triggers.description: This trigger takes an required nonnegative ID number as an argument. If the player's last projectile to make any kind of contact was guarded by the opponent and had the specified ID number, then ProjGuardedTime returns the number of ticks since that contact occurred. If the specified ID number is 0, then the projectile ID is not checked. If no projectile meets all the above conditions, then ProjGuardedTime returns -1.
triggers.args: **exprn** Expression evaluating to a nonnegative ID number (int).
triggers.example:
trigger1 = ProjGuardedTime(1234) = 1
; Triggers if a projectile with ID 1234 was just guarded by the opponent.

trigger1 = ProjGuardedTime(0) != -1 && ProjGuardedTime(0) < 15
; Triggers if any of the player's projectiles was guarded by the opponent within the last 15 ticks.

triggers.name: ProjHit
triggers.description: This trigger takes an optional positive ID number as a suffix. If the ID number is omitted, ProjHit returns true if any of the player's projectiles successfully hit the opponent. When the ID number is specified, ProjHit returns true only if one of the player's projectiles with the specified ID number successfully hit the opponent.
triggers.details: ProjHit will trigger once for each hit of the projectile, so a multi-hit projectile can trigger multiple times. The first form of ProjHit shown above is only valid for one tick after hit, unlike MoveHit. For the second form, ProjHit returns true if the projectile hit n ticks ago, where n is a nonnegative number satisfying the relation "n [oper] value2". Specifying an ID number of 0 gives the same behavior as if the ID number is omitted (check all projectiles).
triggers.example:
trigger1 = ProjHit1234 = 1
; Triggers if a projectile with ID 1234 just made successful contact with the opponent.

trigger1 = ProjHit1234 = 1, < 15
; Triggers if any of the player's projectiles made successful contact with the opponent within the last 15 ticks.

triggers.name: ProjHitTime
triggers.description: This trigger takes an required nonnegative ID number as an argument. If the player's last projectile to make any kind of contact successfully hit the opponent and had the specified ID number, then ProjHit returns the number of ticks since that contact occurred. If the specified ID number is 0, then the projectile ID is not checked. If no projectile meets all the above conditions, then ProjHitTime returns -1.
triggers.args: *exprn* Expression evaluating to a nonnegative ID number (int).
triggers.example:
trigger1 = ProjHitTime(1234) = 1
; Triggers if a projectile with ID 1234 just made successful contact with the opponent.

trigger1 = ProjHitTime(0) != -1 && ProjHitTime(0) < 15  
; Triggers if any of the player's projectiles made successful contact with the opponent within the last 15 ticks.

triggers.name: ProjVar
triggers.description: Returns the specified projectile parameter. Use -1 for ID to iterate over all projectiles.
triggers.args: id Expression 1 index Expression 2 param Valid values are accel x, accel y, angle, angle x, angle y, anim, animelem, animprefix (nightly build only), attr, drawpal.group, drawpal.index, guardflag, highbound, hitflag, layerno, lowbound, pausemovetime, pos x, pos y, projcancelanim, projedgebound, projhitanim, projhits, projID, projmisstime, projpriority, projremove, projremovetime, projremanim, projstagebound, remvelocity x, remvelocity y, scale x, scale y, shader, shadow r, shadow g, shadow b, sprpriority, teamside, vel x, vel y, velmul x, velmul y
triggers.example:
trigger1 = ProjVar(1000, 0, vel Y) > 0
trigger2 = ProjVar(2000, 0, attr) = SCA, HP
trigger3 = ProjVar(3000, 0, guardflag) = L

triggers.name: Rad
triggers.description: Converts an argument value from degree to radians.
triggers.example: trigger1 = Rad(Angle) > pi*0.5

triggers.name: Random
triggers.description: Returns a random number between 0 and 999, inclusive.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = Random <= 249  
; Triggers if the random number returned is less than or equal to  
  249. (This occurs with 25% probability.)

triggers.name: RandomRange
triggers.description: Generates pseudo-random integer numbers uniformly distributed between the given range (both bounds inclusive).
triggers.args: lower Lower range (inclusive) upper Upper range (inclusive)
triggers.example:
type = Explod
trigger1 = RandomRange(var(3), 666) > 100
pos = RandomRange(-300, 600), 0

triggers.name: ReceivedDamage
triggers.description: Returns the total damage dealt by the opposite team to this character, in the currently ongoing combo. This value is valid as long as the opposite team combo count stays above 0, otherwise it returns 0 too.
triggers.example: trigger1 = ReceivedDamage > (LifeMax / 10)

triggers.name: ReceivedHits
triggers.description: Returns the total number of hits done by the opposite team to this character, in the currently ongoing combo. Unlike GetHitVar(hitcount), it takes into account all hits, including those applied by HitAdd. This value is valid as long as the opposite team combo count stays above 0, otherwise it returns 0 too.
triggers.example: trigger1 = ReceivedHits > 10

triggers.name: RedLife
triggers.description: Returns the amount of [red life](https://github.com/ikemen-engine/Ikemen-GO/wiki/Miscellaneous-Info#redlife) the player has.
triggers.example: trigger1 = RedLife = 0

triggers.name: ReversalDefAttr
triggers.description:
Checks the attribute parameter of the player's currently-active ReversalDef. If the player does not currently have an active ReversalDef, then no parameters will match. Can be used for AI to detect a counter or to code something to happen if it exists.

Note: ReversalDefAttr != value1, value2 is logically equivalent to !(ReversalDefAttr = value1, value2).
triggers.args: [oper] =, != value1 A string that has at least one of the letters "S", "C" and "A" for standing, crouching and aerial attacks respectively. For example, "SA" is for standing and aerial attacks. value2 A set of 2-character strings, separated by commas. Each 2-character string must be of the form described: The first character is either "N" for "normal", "S" for "special", or "H" for "hyper". The second character must be either "A" for "attack" (a normal hit attack) or "T" for "throw". For example, "NA, ST" is for normal attacks and special throws. Assuming the attribute of the player's ReversalDefAttr is in the form: arg1, arg2 then the trigger condition is determined to be true only if arg1…
triggers.example:
trigger1 = ReversalDefAttr = A, HA
  Triggers when the player activates a ReversalDef with the following attributes:  
    1. player will reverse an aerial attack
    2. player will reverse a hyper (super) attack

trigger1 = ReversalDefAttr = SC, NA, SA
  Triggers when the player activates a ReversalDef with the following attributes:
    1. player will reverse both standing and crouching attacks
    2. player will reverse both normal and special attacks

triggers.name: RightEdge
triggers.description: RightEdge returns the x position of the right edge of the screen, in absolute stage coordinates.
triggers.details: This trigger is equivalent to the expression CameraPos X + GameWidth / 2.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = Pos X + CameraPos X > RightEdge  
; Triggers if the player is to the right of the right edge of the screen.

triggers.name: RootDist
triggers.description: This trigger is only valid for helper-type characters. RootDist returns the distance from the helper to its root. The root is the main player character who owns the helper: for instance, if you select Kumquat to play with, and Kumquat spawns a helper named Kiwi, who in turn spawns a helper named Penguin, then Penguin's root is Kumquat, and Penguin is a descendant of Kumquat. RootDist works similarly to P2Dist.
triggers.details: For comparing the Y-distance, RootDist gives the difference in the heights of the players' Y-axes. A negative value means that the root is above its descendant. For comparing the X-distance, ParentDist gives the X-distance of the root's axis from the descendant's axis. A positive value indicates the root is in front of its descendant.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = RootDist X != 0  
; Triggers if the root is not at the exact same x-position as the helper character.
changeNotes: The `RootDist` trigger now also accepts a `Z` argument. Returns the distance between the helper and its root in the Z axis.

triggers.name: Round
triggers.description: Returns the rounded value of `val` to specified `precision` (number of digits after the decimal point). `precision` can also be negative or zero.
triggers.args: val Expression evaluating to the value to round. precision Expression evaluating to the number of decimal digits to round to. If the precision is positive, the rounding will occur after the decimal point. If the precision is negative, the rounding will occur before the decimal point. If the absolute value of the precision is greater than or equal to the number of digits, the result of the rounding is equal to 0.
triggers.example: trigger1 = Round(var(3), -2) > 100

triggers.name: RoundNo
triggers.description: Returns the current round number.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = RoundNo = 3  
; Triggers if this is the third round of the match.

triggers.name: RoundsExisted
triggers.description: Returns the number of rounds the player has existed for. On the first round, returns 0. This is useful for a Turns mode intro.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = RoundsExisted = 0  
trigger1 = TeamMode = Turns  
trigger1 = RoundNo > 0  
; Triggers if the player has just entered a Turns mode team match after the first round.
; You can use this example with a ChangeState controller to switch to an intro state by overriding the Initialize state (state 5900).

triggers.name: RoundState
triggers.description: Returns the current round state number.
triggers.details: Return values: 0: Pre-intro  - screen fades in 1: Intro 2: Fight - players do battle 3: Pre-over - just a round is won or lost 4: Over - win poses
triggers.example:
trigger1 = RoundState = 2  
; Triggers if the actual fighting portion of the round is in  
  progress.
changeNotes: The `RoundState` trigger no longer returns 2 during the "Fight!" screen, before players have control, returning 1 instead. `RoundState = 2` is generally understood and documented as the main part of the fight, so this oddity only caused trouble in Mugen.

triggers.name: RoundsWon
triggers.description:
Returns how many total rounds the teamside has won during the current match. Resets between matches.

[TODO]

triggers.name: RoundTime
triggers.description: Returns the tick count since the start of the round.
triggers.example: trigger1 = RoundTime > 600

triggers.name: RunOrder
triggers.description: At the start of each frame, players are sorted into a list for code processing based on their current actions (see [character processing order](https://github.com/ikemen-engine/Ikemen-GO/wiki/Miscellaneous-info#character-processing-order)). `RunOrder` returns their position in this list as an integer.

triggers.name: Scale
triggers.description: Returns the value of the player's drawing scale. `Scale X` and `Scale Y` refer to the scale applied by `AngleDraw`. `Scale Z` refers to the rescaling that affects the player when moving in the Z space.
triggers.example: trigger1 = Scale x > 2 && Scale y > 1

triggers.name: Score
triggers.description: Returns the score points gained in this round by all team members.
triggers.example: trigger1 = Score > 10000

triggers.name: ScoreTotal
triggers.description: Returns the total score points value. Takes into account all team members, previous rounds and previous matches since the start of this game mode.
triggers.example: trigger1 = ScoreTotal > 1000000

triggers.name: ScreenHeight
triggers.description: Returns the height of the screen space in the player's local coordinate space.
triggers.details: ScreenWidth and ScreenHeight are not affected by the camera zoom factor.
triggers.example:
type = Explod  
space = screen  
pos = 0, ScreenHeight  
...  
  Creates an explod in screen-space in the lower-right corner  
  of the screen.

triggers.name: ScreenPos
triggers.description: Gets the value of the player's position relative to the top-right corner of the screen.
triggers.details: For ScreenPos X, the value is relative to the left of the screen (value 0). Negative is left, positive is right. For ScreenPos Y, the value is relative to the top of the screen. Negative is above the screen, positive is downward.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = ScreenPos Y >= 0 && ScreenPos Y < GameHeight  
; True when the player's is in the screen's vertical extent.

triggers.name: ScreenWidth
triggers.description: Returns the width of the screen space in the player's local coordinate space.
triggers.details: ScreenWidth and ScreenHeight are not affected by the camera zoom factor.
triggers.example:
type = Explod  
space = screen  
pos = ScreenWidth / 2, ScreenHeight / 2  
...  
  Creates an explod in screen-space in the center of the screen.

triggers.name: SelfAnimExist
triggers.description: Like AnimExist, except that this only checks P1's animation data. If P1 has been given P2's animation data by a hit, SelfAnimExist will not check P2's animation data to determine whether or not a given action exists.

triggers.name: SelfCommand
triggers.description: [TODO]

triggers.name: SelfStatenoExist
triggers.description: Checks for the existence of a state only within P1's state numbers, even when P1 is custom stated by a hit. Returns 1 if there is a statedef with the specified number. Otherwise it returns 0. Use the statedef number you want to recognize in parentheses.
triggers.args: exprn An expression evaluating to a state number (int).
triggers.example:
trigger1 = !SelfStatenoExist(200)
  ;Triggers if the player is missing state 200.

triggers.name: Shader
triggers.description: Returns the name of the custom shader applied to the player. If no custom shader is applied, "" is returned.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = shader != ""
  ;Triggers if any shader is applied to the player.

triggers.name: Sign
triggers.description: Returns the sign of a real number. If value < 0 return -1. If value 0 return 0. if value > 0 return 1.
triggers.example: var(0) = var(0)*Sign(vel x)

triggers.name: Sin
triggers.description: Computes the sine of the specified argument (in radians.)
triggers.args: **exprn** Expression to compute the sine of. (float)
triggers.example:
value = sin(pi/2)  
; Sets value to the sine of pi/2, which is approximately 1.0 (possibly with some rounding error.)

triggers.name: SoundVar
triggers.description:
Returns the specified sound channel parameter. Use -1 for channelNo to find the first sound available.

**Warning: The results of this trigger are NOT network-safe due to the asynchronous nature of sound playback. Usage of this trigger in production environments is discouraged.**
triggers.args: channelNo Expression param Valid values are group, number, freqmul, isplaying, length, loopcount, loopstart, loopend, pan, position, priority, samplerate (nightly build only), startposition, volumescale
triggers.example:
var(0) = SoundVar(0, IsPlaying)
fvar(1) = SoundVar(1, VolumeScale)

triggers.name: SpritePlayerNo
triggers.description: Returns the player number of the owner of the player's current sprite. Normally returns the same number as the player's player number, but when for instance `ChangeAnim2` is used in a custom state, it will return the number of who owns that sprite.
triggers.example: trigger1 = Player(SpritePlayerNo), SelfAnimExist(1234)

triggers.name: SpriteVar
triggers.description: Returns information about the player's current sprite.
triggers.args: param_name The name of the parameter to check. Valid values are: Group, Height, Image, Width, XOffset, YOffset
triggers.example:
; top left corner of sprite
pos = -SpriteVar(xoffset), -SpriteVar(yoffset)
; lower right corner of sprite
pos = -SpriteVar(xoffset) + SpriteVar(width), -SpriteVar(yoffset) + SpriteVar(height)

triggers.name: SprPriority
triggers.description: Returns the player's/helper's current SprPriority value.
triggers.example: trigger1 = SprPriority > 0

triggers.name: StageBackEdgeDist
triggers.description: Returns the distance to the stage edge (corner) behind the player.
triggers.example: trigger1 = StageBackEdgeDist < 100

triggers.name: StageBGVar
triggers.description: Returns information about the stage's BG elements.
triggers.args: ID The ID of the element to be checked index The index of the element to be checked param The parameter to check. See details
triggers.details:
* actionno: Returns the animation number for type = anim elements (int)
* animelem: Returns the current animation element (int) (nightly build only)
* animelemtime: Returns the current animation element time (int) (nightly build only)
* animloopcount: Returns the number of times the animation has looped (int) (nightly build only)
* animtime: Returns time until animation ends (int) (nightly build only)
* delta.x: Returns the X delta (float)
* delta.y: Returns the Y delta (float)
* id: Returns the ID (int)
* layerno: Returns the layer number (int)
* pos.x: Returns the X position in relation to the starting position (float)
* pos.y: Returns the Y position in relation to the starting position…
triggers.example: trigger1 = StageBGVar(4, 1, actionno) = 40

triggers.name: StageConst
triggers.description: Returns the value of one of the stage's constants. Stage constant variables can be set under stage's DEF [[Constants]](Stage-features/#constants) section.
triggers.args: param_name The name of the constant to check (string).
triggers.example: trigger1 = StageConst(WaterGround) = 1

triggers.name: StageFrontEdgeDist
triggers.description: Returns the distance to the stage edge (corner) in front of the player.
triggers.example: trigger1 = StageFrontEdgeDist < 100

triggers.name: StageTime
triggers.description: Returns the stage's internal time, or the amount of ticks since the last stage reset. The value returned by this trigger corresponds directly to the amount of times stage backgrounds have been updated (taking into account `pausebg`, `resetbg`, etc), allowing one to for instance reliably synchronize [attachedchar](https://github.com/ikemen-engine/Ikemen-GO/wiki/Stage-features#info_attachedchar) actions to what's currently displayed by the stage.
triggers.example: trigger1 = StageTime > 600

triggers.name: StageVar
triggers.description: Returns information about the stage. A limited number of parameters are supported.
triggers.args: **param_name** **The name of the stage parameter to check. Valid values are:** info.name, info.displayname, info.authorname. **[oper]** =, != (other operators not valid) **"string" (string)** String to compare against. Must be in double quotes.
triggers.details:
- info.author: Compares the value of the "author" parameter in the [Info] group. (boolean)
- info.displayname: Compares the value of the "displayname" parameter in the [Info] group. (boolean)
- info.name: Compares the value of the "name" parameter in the [Info] group. (boolean)
**Versions:** 1.0 and newer
triggers.example:
trigger1 = StageVar(info.author) = "Suika"  
; Returns true if the stage author is named "Suika".
changeNotes: A comparison is no longer mandatory. When used bare, `StageVar` returns the stage's name, display name or author name as a string, so it can be compared against another string instead of only a literal. The old syntax is still supported.

triggers.name: Standby
triggers.description: Returns 1 if character is under standby effect (assigned by [TagOut](sctrl#new_tagout) sctrl).
triggers.example: trigger1 = !Standby

triggers.name: StateNo
triggers.description: Returns the player's current state number. Useful for "move interrupts" in the CMD file.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = stateno = [200,650]  
; Returns true if the state number is between 200 and 650, inclusive.

triggers.name: StateType
triggers.description: StateType gives the player's state-type. Refer to the section on StateDef in the CNS documentation for more details on StateType. Useful for "move interrupts" in the CMD file.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = StateType != A  
; Triggers if the player is not in an air-type state.
changeNotes: A comparison is no longer mandatory. When used bare, `StateType` now returns a state type string in the form `"S"`. The old syntax is still supported.

triggers.name: SysFVar
triggers.description: This trigger takes a mandatory variable number as an argument. It returns the value of the player's specified system float variable. This trigger should NOT be used under normal circumstances. System variables are reserved for bookkeeping in common1.cns.
triggers.args: **exprn** An expression evaluating to a variable number. ~~Valid numbers at this time are 0-4.~~
triggers.example:
trigger1 = SysFVar(0) = -1.23  
; Triggers if the value of system float variable 0 is -1.23.

triggers.name: SysVar
triggers.description: This trigger takes a mandatory variable number as an argument. It returns the value of the player's specified system int variable. This trigger is NOT to be used under normal circumstances. System variables are reserved for bookkeeping in common1.cns.
triggers.args: **exprn** An expression evaluating to a variable number. ~~Valid numbers at this time are 0-4.~~
triggers.example:
trigger1 = SysVar(0) = -34  
; Triggers if the value of system variable 0 is -34.

triggers.name: Tan
triggers.description: Computes the tangent of the specified argument (in radians).
triggers.args: **exprn** Expression to compute the tangent of. (float)
triggers.example:
value = tan(pi/4)  
  Sets value to the tangent of pi/4, which is approximately 1.0  
  (possibly with some rounding error.)

triggers.name: TeamLeader
triggers.description:
Returns [playerno](triggers#playerno) of the character that is considered a team leader. In modes where only one player is controlled in particular round (*single*, *turns* and *ratio*) it will be either 1 or 2, depending on team side. In *simul* and *tag* modes, team leader is the first party member (again 1 or 2) by default, but who is considered a leader can be also dynamically adjusted via optional [TagIn](sctrl#new_tagin) sctrl *leader* parameter.

Manually swapping leader changes lifebar elements assignment - leader always uses P1 (or P2, depending on team side) lifebar elements, remaining players positions are moved accordingly, in ascending players order.
triggers.example: trigger1 = TeamLeader = PlayerNo

triggers.name: TeamMode
triggers.description: TeamMode gives the current mode of play for the player's team.
triggers.details: In survival mode, TeamMode = turns on the enemy side.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = TeamMode = Single  
; Triggers if the player is playing in single play.
changeNotes: A comparison is no longer mandatory. When used bare, `TeamMode` returns the current mode as a string directly, which can be read by another trigger or displayed. The old syntax is still supported.

triggers.name: TeamSide
triggers.description: Returns the team side the player is on. 1 represents P1 side (left), 2 for P2 side (right).
triggers.example:
trigger1 = TeamSide = 2  
; Triggers if player is on the P2 side team.

triggers.name: TeamSize
triggers.description: Returns character's team size (for *turns* mode it returns information that was previously not obtainable, for other team modes the returned value is equivalent to using `NumPartner + 1`)
triggers.example: trigger1 = TeamSize = 4

triggers.name: TicksPerSecond
triggers.description: Returns the number of ticks per second. Useful for time calculations.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = Time > 10 * TicksPerSecond  
; Triggers after 10 seconds, regardless of game speed.

triggers.name: Time
triggers.description: Returns the state-time of the player (that is, the number of ticks that the player has been in the current state so far).
triggers.example:
trigger1 = Time = 2  
; Triggers when the player's state-time is 2.

triggers.name: TimeElapsed
triggers.description: Returns the amount of clock ticks since the battle began (0 if time is disabled). Value returned by this trigger corresponds to lifebar timer (only ticks during RoundState = 2)
triggers.example: trigger1 = TimeElapsed > 600

triggers.name: TimeMod
triggers.description: Returns the remainder when the state-time of the player is divided by the specified value. The `%` operator subsumes the functionality of `TimeMod`, so it is recommended that you use `%` instead.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = TimeMod = 4, 3  
; Triggers when the state-time is 3, 7, 11, 15, ...

triggers.name: TimeRemaining
triggers.description: Returns the amount of clock ticks until time over (-1 if time is disabled). Value returned by this trigger corresponds to lifebar timer (only ticks during RoundState = 2)
triggers.example: trigger1 = TimeRemaining > 600

triggers.name: TimeTotal
triggers.description: Returns the total number of clock ticks that have elapsed so far. Takes into account previous rounds and matches since the start of this game mode.
triggers.example: trigger1 = TimeTotal > 5940

triggers.name: TopBoundBodyDist
triggers.description: Like `TopBoundDist`, except this trigger accounts for the player's top `edge` parameter, as defined by the `Depth` state controller.

triggers.name: TopBoundDist
triggers.description: TopBoundDist gives the distance between the player's z-axis and the `topbound` limit of the stage.
triggers.example: trigger1 = TopBoundDist < 40

triggers.name: TopEdge
triggers.description: TopEdge returns the y position of the top edge of the screen, in absolute stage coordinates.
triggers.details: This trigger is equivalent to the expression Pos Y - ScreenPos Y.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = Pos Y > TopEdge  
; Triggers if the player is below the top edge of the screen.

triggers.name: UniqHitCount
triggers.description: Returns the total number of hits the player's current attack move has done. This value is valid only for a single state; after any state change, it resets to 0. To prevent it from resetting to 0, set hitcountpersist in the StateDef (see cns documentation for details). The HitCount and UniqHitCount triggers differ only when the player is hitting more than one opponent. In the case where the player is hitting two opponents with the same attack, HitCount will increase by 1 for every hit, while UniqHitCount increases by 2.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = UniqHitCount = [4,6]  
; Triggers when 4, 5 or 6 hits have been dealt since the start of the player's attack move.

triggers.name: Var
triggers.description: This trigger takes a mandatory variable number as an argument. It returns the value of the player's specified int variable.
triggers.args: **exprn** An expression evaluating to a variable number. ~~Valid numbers at this time are 0-59.~~
triggers.example:
trigger1 = Var(0) = -34  
; Triggers if the value of variable 0 is -34.

triggers.name: Vel
triggers.description: Gets the value of the player's velocity. You must specify the component that you want to check, eg. `Vel Y` to check the Y-velocity.
triggers.details: For Vel X, a positive value indicates that the player is moving forward. (This behavior is the opposite of HitVel X's behavior.) For Vel Y, a positive value indicates that the player is moving downward.
triggers.example:
trigger1 = Vel Y >= 0  
; True when the player is not moving upward.

triggers.name: Win
triggers.description:
Returns true if the player (or the player's team, in team mode) has won the round, false otherwise. Can be suffixed with "KO", "Time", or "Perfect" to return true only when the round has been won by a KO, by time expiring, or with no life lost, respectively.

Format: 1. Win 2. WinKO 3. WinTime 4. WinPerfect
triggers.example:
trigger1 = Win  
; Triggers if the player (or his team) has won the round.  
  
trigger1 = !WinKO  
; Triggers if the player (or his team) has not won the round by a KO. For example, this will trigger if the player's team has not yet won the round, or if they have won the round by time over.

triggers.name: WinClutch
triggers.description: Returns true if the player (or the player's team, in team mode) has won the round with health below the limit set by ``clutch.threshold`` in fight.def. If the parameter isn't defined, the default is under 10%.

triggers.name: WinHyper
triggers.description: Returns true if the player (or the player's team, in team mode) has won the round with the finishing blow being a hyper attack.
triggers.example: trigger1 = !WinHyper

triggers.name: WinKO
triggers.description:
Returns true if the player (or the player's team, in team mode) has won the round, false otherwise. Can be suffixed with "KO", "Time", or "Perfect" to return true only when the round has been won by a KO, by time expiring, or with no life lost, respectively.

Format: 1. Win 2. WinKO 3. WinTime 4. WinPerfect
triggers.example:
trigger1 = Win  
; Triggers if the player (or his team) has won the round.  
  
trigger1 = !WinKO  
; Triggers if the player (or his team) has not won the round by a KO. For example, this will trigger if the player's team has not yet won the round, or if they have won the round by time over.

triggers.name: ZoomVar
triggers.description: Allows checking the scale, pos x, pos y, lag, and remaining time of the currently Zoom sctrl.
triggers.args: param_name The name of the variable to check. Valid values are: scale, pos.x, pos.y, lag, time
triggers.example:
trigger1 = ZoomVar(scale) < 0.9
trigger2 = ZoomVar(pos.x) >= 100
